title: Summit and font (Sacrosanctum Concilium 10)
hook: the liturgy is the summit toward which everything moves and its source
tomorrow: the priest does the praying. so what's left for the pew?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Dei Verbum 21: scripture honored like the Lord's body, both served from one table. The line was word and body.

Sunday night can feel like the top of something, and Monday at seven a.m. like the bottom of a well. A mountain has two famous places: the peak everyone climbs toward, and the spring somewhere on its slope where the river begins. Usually they're different spots. Sacrosanctum Concilium, the council's document on the liturgy, says that in the Church's life they're the same place.
screen: `SUNDAY HIGH, MONDAY LOW.` → `THE PEAK AND THE SPRING.` → `THE SAME PLACE?`

segments.voice: Start with a careful step the council takes just before. Paragraph nine says the liturgy doesn't exhaust everything the Church does: there's preaching, conversion, works of love. So paragraph ten isn't saying nothing else matters. It's saying where everything is headed. That's the summit. All the Church's work, the paragraph says, aims at this: that people made children of God by faith and baptism come together, praise God in the midst of the Church, take part in the sacrifice, and eat the Lord's supper. The soup kitchen and the catechism class both point uphill, toward that gathering. Now the font. The same liturgy is where the Church's strength flows from. From the liturgy, and above all the Eucharist, grace pours out, the council says, as from a fountain. People leave Mass and go back down the mountain carrying water. Put the two together and you get a loop, not a ladder. The week flows toward the altar, and the altar sends the week back out, and then the week climbs back up. Last, why the council bothered to say it. The paragraph ties the liturgy to living: those fed by these sacraments are urged to be one in holiness and to hold on, in their lives, to what they've received in faith.
screen: `THE LITURGY ISN'T EVERYTHING.` · `THE SUMMIT: WHERE IT ALL HEADS.` · `THE FONT: WHERE STRENGTH FLOWS.` · `A LOOP, NOT A LADDER.` · then, large: `SUMMIT AND FONT.`

segments.voice: Make a small plan in three steps. Name one gathering where you're fed and sent back out: Mass this week if you go, or another place if you don't. Name what usually gets in the way, then one small move that clears it, and rest on that plan until the sit ends.
Summit and font. The council's picture of the liturgy: the peak the Church's life climbs toward, and the spring it flows from. Today's word.
Hold onto this: summit and font, uphill to the altar and back down carrying water. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics gather for Mass on Sundays and holy days, and some go during the week; parishes often describe their outreach and teaching as flowing from, and leading back to, the Mass.

chat.meaning: Sacrosanctum Concilium 10 calls the liturgy both summit and font: the week climbs toward it, and its strength flows back out, again and again.

Sacrosanctum Concilium.meaning: Vatican II's constitution on the liturgy; Latin for this sacred council

liturgy.meaning: the Church's public worship, above all the Mass

Eucharist.meaning: the bread and wine of Mass, for Catholics the body and blood of Christ

font.meaning: a spring or fountain; also the basin used for baptism

sources.work: Second Vatican Council, Constitution on the Sacred Liturgy
